newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed mixed to firmer on Thursday, recovering from early weakness after news the Bundesbank left German interest rates unchanged after its regular meeting, dealers said.
"The Bundesbank news was expected but it helped a little bit as did some figures out of the U.S.," said one dealer referring to a rise in U.S. jobless claims in the latest week.

The AEX share index closed 1.65 points higher at 608.24, reversing an early decline to 603.09 but back from the day's high of 610.87. The all-time high of 611.80 was reached on Tuesday, while the closing high of 610.04 was set on Monday.

Dealers said the early move down to the session's low ignored yet another rise to record levels on Wall Street on Wednesday, highlighting sentiment that the Dutch market was beginning to look a little overbought.
"It's getting a bit pyschological now," said one dealer, "People don't think the market's going to keep going up so they're taking profits and waiting to see."

One chart analyst pointed out that the 90-day moving average on the AEX was around 569, well below Thursday's 608.24 point close. "If you're that far from your moving average that's a pretty good signal that the market's overbought," he said.

"If you took an extreme case you could say that maybe we are at the top of a head and shoulders formation here around 610-615," said the chartist. "If you take the first shoulder at around 585 then you can see we could be heading back for a fair correction," he said.
"If we get a new top around 615 then that would be a strong sell. I'm bearish for the first time since July when the index was around 565," the chart analyst said.
The index dumped around 40 points in July when the 90-day moving average rose through the AEX daily trend line, with sentiment hurt by disappointing quarterly company results.

Dealers expressed some concern about the prospects of potentially inflationary U.K. tax cuts ahead of next week's British budget. "There's a chance that interest rates in the U.K. might pick up and that's raising a little scepticism -- people are thinking maybe we've seen the top of this market for a while," another dealer said.

Nine months results from financial group ING were within expectations and were accompanied by a statement from the firm that it saw earnings per share in 1996 some seven to 12 percent higher than in 1995. ING's earnings per share in 1995 were 3.84 guilders, allowing for a share split earlier this year.

ING shares closed 10 cents easier at 58.90 guilders, bouncing from a session low of 57.20 as investors clipped profits ahead of the figures. Some analysts said they would raise their estimates for the year after the nine months results which saw net profit up 24 pct to 2.34 billion guilders.
Food group CSM, which reported full year figures late on Wednesday, closed 3.60 guilders down at 91.80.

"CSM was a little disappointing," said one dealer. "It was within the range but growth in the main businesses was pretty modest," he added. Securities firm Suez Nederland said it was lowering estimates for CSM and reiterated a "hold" rating.
Chemicals firms found renewed demand with Akzo up 4.40 guilders to 221.50 and DSM 1.40 guilders higher at 161.90.

Other leading shares saw Royal Dutch down 2.70 guilders to 283.30, Unilever up 3.10 guilders at 283.70 and Philips 40 cents harder at 63.30 guilders. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
